title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript, Grothendieck's sequel to La Longue Marche. There G is a GL_2-type group, an extension 1 → G_m (its centre) → G → PG → 1. M_{ρ,σ} is a group scheme carrying a homomorphism Θ: M_{ρ,σ} → G and the induced map Θ~: M_{ρ,σ} → PG. ST_ρ and ST_σ are tori attached to the indices ρ and σ. The previous page defines: R = Ker(Θ~) = Θ^{-1}(centre G_m); SR = Ker(Θ); κ: R → G_m with R/SR ≅ G_m; and χ = det∘Θ, with χ|R = κ^2. Earlier numbered statements identify the neutral components: SR° = ST_ρ × ST_σ (62) and R° = R ∩ M° (69).

Diagram (94). This page assembles a 2×3 diagram of inclusions. The top row is SR ⊂ R ⊂ M, with successive quotients G_m and PG. The bottom row is the row of neutral components SR° ⊂ R° ⊂ M°, with the same quotients. Each vertical inclusion has quotient π_0 = μ_2×μ_2. Grothendieck asserts that both squares are cartesian and cocartesian in the group sense. Concretely:
- SR ∩ R° = SR° and R = SR·R°;
- R ∩ M° = R° and M = R·M°.
Hence parallel sides have isomorphic quotients:
- R/SR ≅ R°/SR° ≅ G_m;
- M/R ≅ M°/R° ≅ PG;
- all vertical quotients are μ_2×μ_2.

Prism (95). Adding the composite SR → M, with quotient G (an extension of PG by G_m), gives a prism. Its two triangular faces are the full and neutral-component versions, and its three lateral squares are all bicartesian. Dashed edges point to further subgroups M^+_{ρ,σ} and M^{+°}_{ρ,σ}; these are not explained on this page and are presumably index-2 or 'positive' variants.

Sequence (96). From the diagram he reads off the exact sequence
1 → SR° (= ST_ρ×ST_σ) → R → G_m × μ_2 × μ_2 → 1,
where the map is (κ, ε_i|R, ε_j|R) and the ε's are the sign/component characters. This exhibits R_{ρ,σ} as an extension of a split diagonalizable group G_m×(Z/2)^2 by a product of two tori. The next page continues by building a cube that compares this with an analogous diagram for T_{ρ,σ}, computing intersections such as SR ∩ SG.

Role. This is structural bookkeeping: it determines the 'radical' subgroups of M_{ρ,σ} in terms of very simple groups (tori, G_m, μ_2). It presumably feeds the study of GL_2/PGL_2-valued solutions of the loop equation, i.e. representations of Teichmüller-type fundamental groups.
errors: Gap acknowledged by Grothendieck in the margin note: surjectivity of SR_{ρ,σ} → μ_2×μ_2 (equivalently, the cocartesian property of the left square) still has to be verified. He notes that the corresponding statement for R is known but its transfer to SR is not checked. The claimed bicartesian properties, and hence (96), rest on this.

For (96) to hold one also needs SR ∩ R° to be connected, i.e. equal to SR°. This could fail if the central G_m meets SR in μ_2 outside SR°; the next page's computations of SR∩SG = μ_2 and of the kernels of the cube arrows address exactly this kind of subtlety. It is not justified on this page.
Writing the quotient as a direct product G_m × μ_2 × μ_2 implicitly asserts that the extension R/SR° splits. This is fine because the map is explicitly given by the three characters κ, ε, ε'.

ideas.what: Bicartesian (both pullback and pushout) squares of subgroup inclusions relating a group scheme to its neutral component, giving isomorphic quotients on parallel sides; organized as a prism
ideas.modern_name: Bicartesian squares of normal subgroups / second isomorphism theorem, π_0 of algebraic groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Noether isomorphism theorems; SGA 3 for group schemes)

ideas.what: Structure of the 'radical' R_{ρ,σ}: extension of G_m×μ_2×μ_2 by the torus product ST_ρ×ST_σ
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the preimage of the centre of GL_2 under a representation: tori extended by component groups

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-scheme bookkeeping: neutral components, component groups μ_2×μ_2, and isomorphism theorems inside a larger, unpublished study of the loop equation. Nothing on this page is a new result or a missed connection by itself.
transcription_corrections: Labels: '(90)' above SR_{ρ,σ}, '(86)' above R_{ρ,σ}, '(62)' below SR°, '(69)' below R°; the identification ST_ρ×ST_σ = SR° is written to the left of the bottom row.
Arrow labels G_m and PG denote the quotients of the inclusions; the vertical arrows are labelled μ_2×μ_2 and the squares are labelled 'cart et cocart'.
In (96) the two sign characters are ε-symbols with unclear subscripts (one reads like ε_3, the other is illegible); the transcription's 'ε_3, ε_?' is uncertain.

Margin note (rotated) roughly reads: 'NB (94) — il y a une vérification à faire, que SR_{ρ,σ} → μ_2×μ_2 qui se déduit de celui pour R_{ρ,σ} est surjectif ... mais la vérification [que] R_{ρ,σ} → μ_2×μ_2 ... [à faire]'.

Sentence after (95): '...en forme de prisme dont les trois carrés latéraux sont à la fois cartésiens et cocartésiens — donc donnent lieu à des quotients (sur des côtés parallèles) isomorphes — les quotients qui interviennent étant μ_2×μ_2, G_m, PG et l'extension G de PG par G_m.'
